job.style: a conversation between a teacher and two students

passage: Teacher: Today, let us discuss salts. Many students think 'salt' only means common table salt, but in chemistry, any ionic compound formed by the reaction of an acid and a base is a salt. Rahul: Does that mean all salts have a pH of 7? Teacher: Not necessarily. Depending on the strength of the reacting acid and base, a salt can be acidic, basic, or neutral. Priya: I thought neutralisation meant the acid and base disappear completely. Teacher: That is a common misunderstanding. Neutralisation is a chemical reaction where the properties of the acid and base are neutralised to form salt and water, but the matter is conserved, not destroyed. Rahul: Are all acids dangerous liquids? Teacher: Actually, many acids exist as solids, like citric acid in lemons. Also, while some acids are corrosive, others are essential for life. Finally, remember that bases can be just as dangerous as acids. Many strong bases are highly corrosive and can cause severe chemical burns, even if they feel soapy to the touch. It is a mistake to assume they are harmless just because they are used in cleaning products. Chemistry requires us to look beyond common labels and understand the actual chemical nature of substances.

items.evidence: Many students think 'salt' only means common table salt, but in chemistry, any ionic compound formed by the reaction of an acid and a base is a salt.
items.q: Copper sulphate is never used in cooking. Why do chemists still call it a salt?
options: It forms when an acid reacts with a base
It tastes salty just like kitchen salt
It always has a pH of exactly 7
It is left after acid and base vanish
items.explain: In chemistry, any ionic compound made when an acid reacts with a base is a salt.

wrong.why: thinks salt means only kitchen salt
thinks acid and base disappear in neutralisation

items.evidence: Depending on the strength of the reacting acid and base, a salt can be acidic, basic, or neutral.
items.q: Rahul tests a salt solution and finds its pH is 5. How can this be?
options: It formed from acid and base of unequal strength
It cannot be a salt, as salts are neutral
It must be impure, as neutralisation gives pH 7
It is not salt, since salt means table salt
items.explain: A salt's nature depends on the strength of the acid and base that formed it.

wrong.why: thinks salt means only table salt

items.evidence: Neutralisation is a chemical reaction where the properties of the acid and base are neutralised to form salt and water, but the matter is conserved, not destroyed.
items.q: An acid fully neutralises a base in a beaker. What has happened to their matter?
options: It has changed into salt and water
It has disappeared completely from the beaker
It was destroyed, as the indicator lost colour
It became plain water, as litmus stays unchanged
items.explain: Neutralisation forms salt and water; matter is conserved, not destroyed.

wrong.why: thinks acid and base vanish completely
thinks a colourless indicator means destruction
thinks no litmus change means only water

items.evidence: Actually, many acids exist as solids, like citric acid in lemons.
items.q: Meena finds a white powder labelled citric acid. What does this show about acids?
options: Acids are not always in liquid form
Acids are always dangerous, even as powder
Acids are liquids, so the label is wrong
Acids turn into salts once they dry out
items.explain: Many acids are solids, like citric acid in lemons, so acids are not always liquids.

wrong.why: confuses a solid acid with a salt

items.evidence: Many strong bases are highly corrosive and can cause severe chemical burns, even if they feel soapy to the touch.
items.q: Neha says a strong-base drain cleaner is harmless because it feels soapy. Why is the teacher worried?
options: Strong bases burn skin despite their soapy feel
Soapy bases are harmless, just like bathing soap
Only acids are corrosive, so bases are safe
Only concentrated bases burn, not strong ones
items.explain: Strong bases are highly corrosive and cause severe burns, even though they feel soapy.

wrong.why: thinks only acids can be corrosive
